build: Thalamus's two-sided disk release, G64 images of side A (SHA-256 4544cf5d…) and side B (b30bb735…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection; the title says 1990, the collection 1991 (orientation.md)

comments.text: Characters $00-$08 of chamber 2's character set ($5800-$5842): the chamber's screen_map uses 6 of these 9, $00 most often (352 cells); all multicolour by its char_colours.

Rows 3-6 of character $08, the rope's run along row 8 from the weight to the rats' ledge: rope_run rotates each row left by a multicolour pixel (two bits), so the rope seems to slide towards the weight as it falls. Row 7 ($5847) is not rotated.

Character $09 ($5848-$584F), the cable in column 2 that runs down to the sleeping monster (rows 2-5 and 9-17 of the chamber's screen_map, broken at rows 6-8): ride_step rotates its rows down by one at each step, the old row 7 into row 0 here, so the cable runs down while the platform rises.
Rows 1-6 of character $09, moved down a row by ride_step.
Row 7 of character $09, which ride_step takes to put in row 0.

Character $0A ($5850-$5857), the cable in column 5 (rows 1-20) that the platform rides up: ride_step rotates its rows up by one at each step, row 0 (here) into row 7, so the cable runs up with the platform.
Rows 1-6 of character $0A, moved up a row by ride_step.
Row 7 of character $0A, where ride_step puts the old row 0; then characters $0B and $0C.

Character $0D ($5868-$586F), the rope's drop in column 14 to the weight: rope_run rotates its rows down by one at each call, row 7 into row 0 here, so the rope runs down as the weight falls; rope_lengthen writes this character into the cells below as the weight drops.
Rows 1-6 of character $0D, moved down a row by rope_run.
Row 7 of character $0D, which rope_run takes to put in row 0. The characters after it follow.

Characters $15-$4E of chamber 2's character set ($58AF-$5A77, character $15 from its row 7): the chamber's screen_map uses 56 of these 58, $3F most often (7 cells); 55 multicolour by its char_colours.

Character $4F of the chamber's character set ($5800-$5FFF), and the seven after it. The label is the engine's: wipe_char_set redefines character $4F here for a screen wipe; the chamber never calls it.
Characters $57-$61 of chamber 2's character set ($5AB8-$5B0F): the chamber's screen_map uses all of these, $60 most often (6 cells); all multicolour by its char_colours.

Characters $62-$6B ($5B10-$5B5F), the purple demon that works the mill's drive (rows 18-21, columns 14-16): mill_demon_frame copies the next of eight 80-byte pictures from mill_demon_frames over them every fourth frame while the mill runs. The label covers the first 64 of the 80 bytes.

Characters $71 and $72 ($5B88-$5B97), the top row of the sleeping monster (rows 18-21, columns 0-2, characters $7C, $71-$7B): monster_body copies a 64-byte picture over $71-$78 at each step of the ride up.

Characters $73 and $74 ($5B98-$5BA7), row 19, columns 0 and 1 of the monster: monster_pose copies one of the four 16-byte poses at $8E95-$8ED4 here as the monster dozes off and as it winds the platform up. Then $75-$78, which only monster_body changes.
Character $85 (row 16, column 1, above the sleeping monster): snore_z copies the top of the rising Z into it, a picture from z_frames_lo/hi; torture_start clears it and $86.
Character $86 (row 17, column 1): snore_z copies the lower part of the rising Z into it. The characters after it follow.

Row 0 of character $C4, the top edge of the conveyor belt (row 15, columns 21-32): each belt step rotates this byte a multicolour pixel right, towards the saw, or left while the belt runs back. The rest of characters $C4 and $C5 follow.
Row 7 of character $C5, the lower edge of the belt (row 16, columns 21-23): each belt step rotates it the opposite way to belt_top_row, so the belt seems to go round. The characters after it follow.

Sprite block $81 (the bank's sprites start at $6000, block $80), the panel's weapon icon: weapon_icon_draw copies the icon's second half into its first 24 bytes (loader_hand_over shows the weapon's icon in a chamber).
Sprite block $82, where weapon_icon_draw copies the weapon icon's first half (24 bytes).
Sprite block $83 of chamber 2's sprites ($60C0-$60E6): $83 one of the panel's weapon icon blocks, which the engine's weapon_icon_draw draws into.
Sprite block $83 from row 13 ($60C0 plus 39), where weapon_icon_draw copies the icon's second half again (24 bytes).
Sprite block $84 from row 13, where weapon_icon_draw copies the icon's first half again.

Sprite blocks $85-$8F of chamber 2's sprites ($6167-$63FF, block $85 from its byte 39): $85-$86 Chaz lying on the floor after his fall (chaz_flash_frames); $87-$88 Chaz falling off the belt's left end (chaz_fall_frames), $87 also lying on the floor; $89 Chaz lying on the belt; $8A-$8B Chaz calling for help (chaz_call_frames), $8A also his struggle at the saw (chaz_sawn flips it with $89); $8C-$8D the weight's two halves; $8E-$8F the saw blade turning (blade_frames).

Sprite blocks $90-$9F of chamber 2's sprites ($6400-$67FF): $90-$91 the saw blade turning (blade_frames); $92 the blood at the saw (blood_frames); $93 the platform's lower sprite (platform_lower); $94-$98 a rat gnawing the rope, facing out (rat_gnaw_frames); $99-$9D a rat walking left (rat_left_frames); $9E-$9F a rat walking right (rat_right_frames).

Sprite blocks $A0-$AF of chamber 2's sprites ($6800-$6BFF): $A0-$A2 a rat walking right (rat_right_frames); $A3 the box of popcorn; $A4-$A6 the box tipping as it falls (box_fall_frames); $A7-$AB the sparks over the mill's motor while Chaz is on the belt (sparks_frames); $AC the platform's upper sprite (platform_upper); $AD-$AF the sparks once Chaz has fallen off (sparks_frames_2).

Sprite blocks $B0-$BF of chamber 2's sprites ($6C00-$6FFF): $B0 the sparks once Chaz has fallen off (sparks_frames_2); $B1-$BF the green monster's two halves walking, spitting and breathing fire (gm_walk_frames, gm_spit_frames).

Sprite blocks $C0-$CF of chamber 2's sprites ($7000-$73FF): $C0-$C2 the green monster's two halves walking, spitting and breathing fire (gm_walk_frames, gm_spit_frames); $C3-$C7 a fireball in flight (fireball_frames); $C8-$CB the fireball dying away (fireball_frames); $CD-$CF the fireball dying away; and $CC is named by no animation script or routine found.

Sprite blocks $D0-$D7 of chamber 2's sprites ($7400-$75F8): $D0 the box open on the lower ledge; $D1-$D6 the popcorn spilling out (popcorn_frames); $D7 the water tank, upright, which the drops fill row by row (tank_sprite_rows).

Row 19 of sprite block $D7, the upright water tank ($75C0-$75FF): torture_start empties rows 7-19 with tank_empty_row, and each water drop that lands adds a row of tank_water_row from row 19 upwards (tank_fill). The bytes after the block are the next sprites.

Sprite blocks $E7-$EF of chamber 2's sprites ($79F9-$7BFF, block $E7 from its byte 57): $E7-$E8 the splash (splash_frames); $E9-$EC the blood spraying at the saw (blood_frames); $ED-$EF Chaz's call for help, its speech bubble (bubble_frame).

Sprite blocks $F0-$FF of chamber 2's sprites ($7C00-$7FFE): $F0 Chaz's call for help, its speech bubble (bubble_frame); $F1-$F4 rat 0 at the popcorn, head down (rat_eat_frames); $F5-$FF the green monster's two halves bursting (gm_burst_frames_a, gm_burst_frames_b).
The last byte of the VIC bank at $4000-$7FFF, which the VIC shows in the open border while idle: the rescue screen sets it to 0.

Cold and warm start vectors for the KERNAL's cartridge test, both $AF6A (memory_wipe), followed at $8004 by the signature CBM80 ($C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30). Every level and chamber file carries them, so a reset while the chamber is in memory runs memory_wipe and erases the game.

The chamber's 15 objects' starting x and y (30 bytes), copied to obj_xy by torture_start; objects_start_msb and the store of $60 into $C25C give the ninth x bits. 0 and 1 the green monster on the top ledge (175,50 and 199,50), 2 and 3 its fireballs, 4 the popcorn box behind it (192,74), 5, 7 and 8 the three rats on the right-hand ledge (238, 258 and 278, all at y 102; rat_x replaces their x), 6 the spilt popcorn (239,102), 9 a second box that no band puts on a sprite, 10 and 11 the 10-ton weight (116,133 and 140,133), 12 Chaz on the belt (208,156), 13 the saw blade (272,150), 14 the sprite beside Chaz (positioned by raster_objects_c).
Sprite 6's x, $B0: the sparks over the mill's motor, drawn by raster_sparks.
Sprite 6's y, $BC.
The splash sprite's x, $20 (32, double width, over the sleeping monster), drawn by raster_tank through splash_sprite.
The splash sprite's y, $CD.
The water tank's x (sprite 5, raster_tank): torture_start sets $59; tank_tip moves it 4 pixels left for each of the first three tipping frames.
The water tank's y, $CD.

The 15 objects' starting sprite frames, copied to obj_frame: $B3 and $B4 the green monster, $0F (blank) for the fireballs, rats, popcorn and sprite 14, $A3 the popcorn box (and object 9), $8C and $8D the weight, $89 Chaz lying on the belt, $4E for the saw blade (saw_and_sparks puts the blade's own frames in from the first frame).

Sprite 6's frame: saw_and_sparks writes it every other frame from sparks_frames ($A7-$AB), or from sparks_frames_2 ($AD-$B0) once Chaz has fallen off the left end; $0F (blank) once the weight is down.
The splash sprite's frame: $0F until tank_tip shows splash_frames.
The water tank's frame: $D7 upright; tank_tip steps it through $D8 and $D9 (tipping over) and $DA-$E1 (draining).

The starting colours of objects 0-12, copied to obj_colour: green for the green monster, light red for the fireballs, the box, object 9 and Chaz, grey for the rats and the weight, yellow for the popcorn.
The starting colour of object 13, the saw blade (grey, $0C; torture_start writes $0C again), then of object 14 (white, $01).
Sprite 6's colour, yellow.
The splash sprite's colour, light blue.
The water tank's colour, light blue.
The chamber's entry point: loader_hand_over jumps here once a torture chamber's file is in (part digit "3"), and the JMP goes on to torture_begin.
Set by belt_step when the belt carries Chaz off its left end (x below $B2): the main loop runs chaz_falling, which ends in a lost life. It also stops the belt moving him.
Set by belt_step when the belt carries Chaz to x $FC, at the saw: the main loop runs chaz_sawn, which ends in a lost life.
ride_step's count, 7 down to 0, between restarts of monster_body's pictures (eight pictures to a cycle).
mill_demon_frame's count of pictures, 7 down to 0, before it starts its eight pictures again.
The sparks' frame index, 5 down to 0 (saw_and_sparks).
The saw blade's frame index, 3 down to 0 (saw_and_sparks).
Set by water_drip when its thirteenth drop has landed and the tank is full: the drips stop and a shot on the tank now tips it.
Set by tank_hit when a shot hits the full, upright tank: the main loop runs tank_tip until the splash ends.
Set by tank_tip when the splash ends: the sleeping monster has woken, and monster_wind winds the platform up.
Set when Clyde steps onto the wound-up platform at the bottom of column 5 (the main loop at $83BA): ride_step lifts him to the top ledge; cleared there.
snore_z's place in snore_z_top and snore_z_bottom.
tank_tip's count, 4 down to 0: a step every fifth frame.
The green monster's place in gm_script.
Set while one of the green monster's moves (gm_x_scripts) is running; gm_walk reads the next byte of gm_script when it is clear.
The read position in the current move's x script.
The read position in the current move's frame script.
Frames between the green monster's frames, 5 down to 0 (every sixth).
Set while the green monster shows frame $C1, so that each showing spits once (gm_spit).
Which fireball the next spit uses, 0 or 1 (objects 2 and 3).
The two fireballs' places in fireball_dx, fireball_dy and fireball_frames; the first also counts the flame's steps (flame_frames_l1 and l2) when the green monster breathes fire.
The three rats' frame indexes, one each, counted down through their frame tables (7 to 0, or 5 to 0 at the popcorn) as the frames change; 9 when a rat changes what it is doing.
What each rat was doing last frame: 0 sitting, 1 walking right, $FF walking left, 2 or 3 at its place by the popcorn.
What each rat is doing this frame (rat_move), compared with rat_state to restart rat_delay.
The green monster's hit flash, 9 down to 0: raster_objects_a colours it from gm_flash_colours.
The damage the green monster has taken: each shot adds the weapon's grade plus one ($129D), and at $C8 (200) it is killed.
Set by gm_hit at 200 damage: gm_walk then sets gm_dying.
Set by gm_walk once the monster is killed: its moves stop, gm_burst plays and the popcorn box can be shot.
Set by box_hit when the shots have pushed the popcorn box to x $D0, off the end of the ledge: box_fall drops it and spills the popcorn.
gm_burst's count, 5 down to 0: a frame every sixth.
Rounds of gnawing: rats 1 and 2 each add one per round of their gnawing frames, and at gnaw_rounds (10) rope_stage_due is set and this starts again.
Set at the tenth round of gnawing: the main loop runs rope_snap, which moves the rope on a stage.
Which stage of rope_snap's rope_stages comes next (0-2).
Set with chaz_fell or chaz_at_saw: the rats stop where they are (rat_target).
Set when chaz_falling or chaz_sawn ends: the main loop takes a life.
Set (to $B8) when the weight hits the ground: the belt, the sparks and the mill demon stop, and the rope stops running.
RUN/STOP pause: set when RUN/STOP is pressed with the joystick still; the loop then skips Clyde and the puzzle until the joystick moves.
Set by gm_burst when its last frame is shown.
The screen shake when the weight lands: set to 7, then raster_objects_a puts shake_scroll's vertical scroll into $D011 each frame, counting down.
Set when the weight lands: after rescue_delay frames the main loop goes to the rescue screen.
The sleeping monster's poses while it winds the platform up, one per step of monster_wind, read from the end (41 entries): 0-3 pick a pose from monster_pose_lo, going back and forth.
monster_wind's steps left, $28 at the start; at 0 the platform is wound up and Clyde can ride it.
The popcorn box's frames as it falls (box_fall, read from the end): $A4, $A5 and $A6 tipping, five frames each, then $D0, open on the lower ledge.
The box's x step for each fall step: 1 and 0 in turn.
The box's y step for each fall step, read from the end: 1 and 0 at first, up to 4 at the end.
box_fall's steps left, $12 (18) at the start.
How far the weight falls each frame (weight_fall, by weight_fall_step): read from index $0E down to 0, so 1, 1, 2, 2 and up to 7 pixels, then 8 (index 0) for the rest of the fall.
The index into weight_fall_dy: $0F at the start, one less each frame of the fall down to 1; from then on weight_fall reads index 0.
The three bands' ninth x bits, copied to obj_x_msb: only the third band's $40, object 13 (the saw blade) past x 255. torture_start then writes $60 into the second band's byte ($C25C).
The three bands' multicolour bits, copied to sprite_mc_bands: $F8, $F8 and $3F.

Sets the chamber up (also after a lost life, from retry_screen): clears the variables $8054-$8081 and the Z characters, sets the bands' ninth x bits and multicolour, the rats' x, turns round the engine's tests of solid characters (solid_test_bcs, solid_test_bcc), sets the mill demon's, the monster's and its body's first pictures, then copies the screen from screen_map ($9BE7) into $4400 with each character's colour from char_colours, colours column 9 light blue from row 11 down (the drips' column), empties the water tank, and sets the engine for a chamber ($126C, $1216, $120C, shot_y_max $CF, Clyde's dying count $ED, player_x_min $18 and limit $41, object_collisions' slot settings $12DE, $12E6 and $12EA), the puzzle's counts and scripts, the 15 objects, Clyde at (298,205), the music and the raster chain at raster_panel.

Operand of the LDX at $81A2: the screen copy's page count, 3 down to 0, stored at $818A. Then colour RAM from $D9C1 (row 11, column 9) down 11 rows is set light blue, drip_reset points water_drip at row 11, and the counts begin: the drip's first wait $3D and drop count $0C (thirteen drops, $8E64), object 13's colour, snore_z's loop end, the splash's eleven steps, the tank's frame and x, tank_fill's row address ($75F9), the platform's erase address ($4725), the rats' decision time $25, and the empty tank: tank_empty_row written to rows 19 up to 7.
Low byte of the STA operand at $820A (the tank sprite's row, from $F9 down by 3 each row).

High byte of the STA operand at $820A. The rest of torture_start: shot_y_max $CF, the Chaz call's frame $ED and Clyde's dying count $ED, snore_z's first wait $64, the rats' ninth bits ($60 in $C25C), $12EA = $F7, gnaw_rounds 10, the flags set to 1 ($120C, $126C, $1216, $1241, the belt's direction to the right, chaz_sawn's delay, both fireballs idle, the first rope stage), monster_pose's three dozing steps, rope_stages' second count 3 and $12E6, the belt's first wait $32 and the Chaz call's $32, chaz_falling's counts $16, $2C and 5, snore_z's loop start 4, gm_flash_colours' green, chaz_sawn's steps, the popcorn's six steps, player_x_min $18 and limit $41, the objects, Clyde at x $2A past 255, y $CD (and the platform's y), his colour, the lever's colour ($DB45), gm_burst's eight frames, his sprites blank, the two self-modified SECs ($8C96, $98E5), then the tune (tune_start) and the raster chain (irq_install with $01 = $36), from raster_panel at line $F9.

The chamber's main loop, once a frame: RUN/STOP pause, the weapons tablet or Clyde (player_control, player_fire, player_animate, panel_anim; ride_step and riding_sprites instead while he rides the platform), then the puzzle's routines, player_dead or the collision tests, the music, and the end: life_lost or the end of Clyde's dying count takes a life (below zero is game over, through torture_exit), rescued leads to the rescue screen after rescue_delay frames.

The puzzle, unless paused: objects_save_positions, lever, the belt (until the weight is down), the platform (with the winding done, Clyde at x $39, y $C5 with the platform's spot, character $A4, three rows below and one column right of his cell ($8A), starts the ride: riding set, his shots stopped through $1242), chaz_falling or chaz_sawn, the sparks, the blade and the mill demon (or sprite 6 blanked once the weight is down), water_drip until the tank is full, tank_tip, monster_wind, snore_z; the green monster only once the platform has reached the top (character $9E at $44CC): gm_walk unless it is dying (object 1 kept 24 pixels right of object 0), gm_spit, and gm_burst; the three rats (rat_move, copying rat_x and rat_frame into objects 5, 7 and 8), box_fall, rope_snap while the weight hangs.

The end of the frame's work: a lost life (life_lost, or Clyde's dying count $1288 run out) takes one from lives and goes to retry_screen, or to torture_exit when none are left; while rescued is set rescue_delay counts down, and at 0 the rescue screen starts.
Frames from rescued to the rescue screen: $5B (91), counted down by the main loop.
Starts the chamber's tune (torture_tune at $A0CF); the main loop calls it again whenever the tune has ended.

Raster routine at line $E1 (and the chain's first, at line $F9, where irq_install starts it): character multicolours brown and light red, no sprite priority or double height, the score panel's sprites (panel_sprites, or panel_sprites_tablet while the tablet is up), and frame_divider. Next raster_panel_lower at line $F4.

Raster routine at the top of the screen (line 0): the green monster's two halves (objects 0 and 1) take gm_flash_colours' entry for gm_flash, which counts down; sprites_band1 puts objects 0-4 on sprites 3-7, with sprites 3 and 4 (the monster) double height; sprite multicolours dark grey and yellow, character multicolour light green; while shake_step counts, the vertical scroll in $D011 takes shake_scroll's value (the screen shakes). Then clyde_sprites, and next raster_ledge_colour at line $54.
Operand of the ORA at $852E: the vertical scroll for this frame of the shake, from shake_scroll.
The vertical scroll values of the screen shake when the weight lands, read from the end as shake_step counts down: 5, 3, 1, 3, 4, 3, 2, 3 (the usual scroll is 3).
Raster routine at line $54: character multicolour light red for the ledges. Next raster_objects_b at line $5D.

Raster routine at line $5D: objects 5-8 (the rats and the popcorn) on sprites 3-6, with their ninth x bits from $C00B; multicolour for sprites 3, 5, 6 and 7 and Clyde's; sprite 4, the popcorn, double width; priority from the band's bits. Object 9 is left out, so it never shows. Next raster_objects_c at line $7C.

Raster routine at line $7C: sprites_band3 puts objects 10-14 (the weight, Chaz, the saw blade and sprite 14) on sprites 3-7; then places object 14 for the next frame. While Chaz is left of x $F0 it sits 13 pixels right of him (his call for help, double width, coloured by chaz_call through $85CC); once he is at the saw it sits 5 pixels right of him at y $90, red and single width (the blood of chaz_sawn), with the ninth x bits of objects 13 and 14 set. Sprites 3 and 4 (the weight) double height, sprite 6 behind the landscape. Next raster_belt_colour at line $92.
Operand of the LDX at $85CB: sprite 7's colour while object 14 is Chaz's call, written by chaz_call from chaz_call_colours.
Raster routine at line $92: character multicolour grey for the belt and the mill. Next raster_sparks at line $B0.
The LDX of the next routine's low byte ($69, raster_sparks). The label is the engine's: scroll_draw_column and scroll_finish_column read the levels' tile table at $8609, and a chamber never scrolls.
Set while Clyde stands at the lever, so that one arrival flips it once.

The lever at the bottom right (characters at rows 20 and 21, columns 37 and 38): when Clyde is past x 255 at x $39 or more and at y $C8 or below, and was not there last frame, the belt's direction flips, and the lever is redrawn: for the belt running right $83 at row 20, column 38 with $84 and $07 below it, for the belt running left $83 at row 20, column 37 with $81 and $82 below. Clyde leaving clears lever_latch.
Counts down every fourth frame between belt steps: $32 at the start, then $1E (a step every 120 frames). weight_fall keeps writing the weight's y into it, so the belt stops while the weight falls.
The belt's direction: 1 towards the saw (the start), 0 back to the left; lever flips it.

The conveyor belt, every fourth frame: when belt_wait runs out (every 120 frames) the roller at row 15 and 16, column 20 turns a character ($BC-$BF, $C0-$C3), the belt's edges rotate a multicolour pixel (belt_top_row, belt_bottom_row), and unless Chaz has fallen he moves 2 pixels with it: right, he reaches the saw at x $FC (chaz_at_saw); left, off the end below x $B2 (chaz_fell). Both set chaz_gone.
The low byte of the LDA $C25D at $8708 (the third band's ninth x bits). The label is the engine's: scroll_column reads the levels' row pointers at $8709 and $870A.
The high byte of the LDA's address. The label is the engine's, as $8709's.

The offset of the BNE at $8714: past x 255 Chaz has not reached the left end. The label is the engine's: scroll_column and the Get Ready strip ($3B56) read the levels' first map row at $8715. Then: below x $B2 he falls (chaz_fell, chaz_gone).
Chaz's x step as he falls off the left end of the belt, read from the end: 1 and 0 in turn (chaz_falling).
His y step as he falls, read from the end: 1 and 0 at first, up to 3.
His frames as he falls, read from the end: $88 for seven steps, then $87.
chaz_falling's fall steps left, $16 (22); at 0 the sparks change to sparks_frames_2 and chaz_call stops.
chaz_falling's steps left in a round of the flashing, $2C (44).
Rounds of the flashing left, 5.

Each frame once Chaz has gone off the left end of the belt: he falls 22 frames (chaz_fall_dx, chaz_fall_dy, chaz_fall_frames), then lies on the floor for five rounds of 44 frames, his frame from chaz_flash_frames and his colour from chaz_flash_colours, in single colour when the colour is white; then life_lost.
chaz_sawn's count: a step every third frame.
Object 14's frames while Chaz is sawn, read from the end: $92 twice, then $E9-$EC, the spray, over and over.
chaz_sawn's rounds left, $2D (45, written by torture_start): at $14 the blade turns orange, at $13 red, and at 0 a life is lost.
The index into blood_frames: 6 for the first round, 4 for the others.

Each frame once the belt has brought Chaz to the saw: every third frame his frame flips (EOR 3) and object 14 shows the next of blood_frames; after each round sawn_steps counts down, the blade turning orange then red, and at the end life_lost is set.
The LDA #$03 that restarts sawn_delay. The label is the engine's: the Get Ready strip ($3B69) reads the levels' second map row at $87D5.
Sprite 6's frames over the motor while Chaz is on the belt, read from the end: $A9, $AB, $AA, $A9, $A8, $A7.
Sprite 6's frames once Chaz has fallen off the left end: $AE, $AD, $B0, $AF, $AE, $AD.
The saw blade's frames (object 13), read from the end: $8E, $8F, $90, $91.
Every other frame: the sparks' next frame (sparks_frames, or sparks_frames_2 once Chaz has fallen) into sparks_frame, and the saw blade's next frame (blade_frames). Then chaz_call.

On the frames where frame_divider's $121A and $121B are both set (two in eight), unless Chaz has fallen: while the belt carries him towards the saw left of x $F0, chaz_call_wait counts down from $C8; at $1A the call starts, 26 steps of his frame (chaz_call_frames: he lifts his head), object 14's frame (chaz_call_bubble: $0F, or bubble_frame) and its colour (chaz_call_colours, through $85CC); at 0 the wait starts again at $C8 and the next call shows the next bubble.
The store into bubble_frame (wrapping from $F0 to $ED) and the wait set to $C8 again. The label is the engine's: the Get Ready strip ($3B75) reads the levels' third map row at $8895.

The drops that fill the water tank. drip_step counts down by 2: from $3D to $31 every 16th frame, the wait; from $2F to $29 every 16th frame, a drop forming under the ledge at row 11, column 9 (characters $7D, $7E, $7F, $80); then every frame, the drop falling half a row a step (character $80 in a cell, or $04 over $05 across two) to the tank at row 20. drip_chars gives each step's pair of characters. When a drop lands, tank_fill adds a row of water, and after the thirteenth drop tank_full is set.
Low byte of the STA operand at $891C: the drop's cell on the screen, from drip_reset ($45C1, row 11, column 9), moved down a row ($28) each time the drop moves.
High byte of the drop's cell address.

The JSR to panel_lower. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The return with raster_border at line $F9, while the tablet is up. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.

chaz_flash_colours from index 12. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads the address of a level's per-frame routine here (level_frame_call).
chaz_flash_colours from index 14. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_player_call address here.
chaz_flash_colours from index 16. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_jump_call address here.

Index 23 of chaz_flash_colours. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's second strip colour here.
Index 24 of chaz_flash_colours. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's third strip colour here.

Chaz's frame for each step of a flashing round, read from the end: $85, $86 and $87, lying on the floor; $8D35 is not read.

The rescue sign's seven rows of dots, one byte each and a bit per sprite, the top row at $8D3C: matrix_scroll copies each letter of matrix_font in, and raster_rescue_top and raster_rescue_row turn each byte into the sprites shown on that row.

Inside the first text. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup reads a level's tune address, low byte, here.

Inside the second text. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's animation script table (low bytes) here.
"CHAZ OFFERS CLYDE HIS COLLECTION" and $FF, string 7.
"OF MAGIC POTION CREATURES AS REWARD" and $FF, string 8.

The colour of the call for help (object 14) at each of chaz_call's steps, indexed 26 down to 1 ($8E13-$8E2C): black three times, dark grey, grey, light grey, then white for 16 steps, and back out to black. Its first byte, $FF, ends the text before it and is not read as a colour.

chaz_call_bubble from index 3. The label is the engine's: object_kill reads a level's death movement table (x) here.
Chaz's frame at each step of the call, indexed 26 down to 1 ($8E47-$8E60): $8A, then $8B for most of it (head raised), $8A and $89. Its first byte is chaz_call_bubble's last.
chaz_call_frames from index 9. The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_path read a level's death movement table (y) here.

The frame of the next call's bubble, $ED to $F0 in turn.
water_drip's step, counted down by 2 (see water_drip): $3D at the start, $31 after each drop.
The drops left to fall, from $0C: after the drop that takes it below zero the tank is full (thirteen drops). Also read as the lower character of drip_chars' pairs.

water_drip's characters, a pair for each step (index drip_step, the upper cell's character; drip_step minus 1, the lower's): $7D, $7E, $7F and $80 as the drop forms, then $80 (move down a row) and $04 over $05 in turn as it falls, and blanks as it lands.

The last six bytes of drip_chars ($7F, $7E and $7D with zeros), then from $8E95 the monster's four 16-byte poses for characters $73 and $74 (monster_pose): the label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_10 read a level's y movement script table (high bytes) here.
The monster's pose 1 from its 11th byte, then pose 2. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's hit point table here.
Pose 2 from its 11th byte, then pose 3. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's wake-delay table here.
The last six bytes of pose 3. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's table here.

The purple demon working the mill, every fourth frame: copies the next 80-byte picture of mill_demon_frames into characters $62-$6B ($5B10), back to the first after eight. torture_start enters at $8EDF for the first picture.

The entry torture_start uses: mill_demon_delay counts down, and below zero it is 7 again and the source goes back to mill_demon_frames. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's table of hits needed (obj_hit_need, $2201) here.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $8EF5, the picture's address in mill_demon_frames, moved on $50 a picture.
High byte of the mill demon picture's address, moved on with the low byte; the loop copies the picture into mill_demon_chars ($5B10).
The BPL of the copy loop. The label is the engine's: ride_parent reads a level's x offset table here.
The store of the next picture's address. The label is the engine's: ride_parent reads a level's y offset table here.
The RTS. The label is the engine's: object_kill compares the object it is killing with a level's end object here ($149D).
Eight pictures of 80 bytes (characters $62-$6B), the purple demon working the mill, copied in turn by mill_demon_frame.
A row of the water tank full of water (06 AA 90), which tank_fill writes into the tank's sprite as each drop lands.
A row of the empty tank, its two sides only (04 00 10), written by torture_start into rows 7-19 of the tank's sprite.
Writes tank_water_row into the tank's sprite (block $D7) at the row its STA points to, then moves the STA up a row (3 bytes): one row of water for each drop.
Low byte of the STA operand at $9198, the tank sprite's next row to fill: $F9 (row 19) at the start, 3 less after each drop.
High byte of the row's address, $75.
The splash's steps left, $0B at the start (tank_tip).
The splash's frame for each step, read from the end: blank for three steps (while the tank goes over), then $E2 up to $E8, then blank; the last entry is not read.

Every fifth frame once the full tank has been shot: the tank's next frame (tank_frame, up to $E1: over on its side, then draining), moving 4 pixels left with each of the first three; the splash's next frame over the sleeping monster. When the splash ends the monster is awake (monster_awake; tank_tipping cleared), snore_z is sent to its last, blank frames ($92DC $15, $92DD $14), and score value 7 is added (one in the tens digit).

Raster work before the ride (from raster_tank): sprite 3 double width, multicolour for sprites 0-2, 4, 5 and 7; the splash on sprite 3 (splash_sprite), and the platform at the bottom of its cable on sprites 4 and 7 (platform_lower and platform_upper, both at x $38, y platform_y).

The same during the ride (from the main loop, and raster_tank's first frame of it): sprite 7 double width for the splash, multicolour for sprites 0-5, the platform on sprites 1 and 2 (Clyde's shot sprites, which clyde_sprites leaves alone while riding), with their ninth x bits clear.
Puts the splash on sprite 3 + X (position at $D006 + Y): splash_colour, splash_frame, splash_x and splash_y.
Puts the platform's lower sprite on sprite 1 + Y (position at $D002 + X): x $38, y platform_y, frame $93, brown. platform_upper follows.
Puts the platform's upper sprite on sprite 2 + Y (position at $D004 + X): x $38, y platform_y, frame $AC, light red.
Low bytes of the sleeping monster's four 16-byte poses for characters $73 and $74 ($8E95, $8EA5, $8EB5, $8EC5), picked by winding_script.
High bytes of the four poses, all $8E.

Every fourth frame once the monster is awake: winding_steps counts down from $28, and at each step the monster takes the pose winding_script names (monster_pose), winding the platform up. At 0 the platform is ready and Clyde can ride it.
For each of snore_z's steps, which picture of z_frames_lo/hi goes into character $85 (the upper cell): blank for the first four, then pictures 9-16, twice, and blank.
For each step, the picture for character $86 (the lower cell): pictures 1-8 twice, then blank. Read together with snore_z_top, a Z rises out of the lower cell into the upper.
The step at which snore_z goes back to z_loop: $0C while the monster sleeps, $15 once it wakes.
The step snore_z goes back to: 4 while the monster sleeps (steps 4-11 over and over), $14 once it wakes (step 20, blank).
Low bytes of the Z pictures: 0 for picture 0, then $67 and on by 8 for pictures 1-16.
High bytes: $58 for picture 0 (character 0 of the chamber's set, blank), $9B for pictures 1-16 (z_pictures at $9B67).
snore_z's count, every other frame: $64 at the start, then $19 between the monster's dozing poses.
The monster's dozing poses still to come, 2 at the start: each time doze_wait runs out it goes down one and monster_pose shows the next pose; once it is below zero the Z's start.

Every other frame. On the frames where $121A is also set, once the monster has dozed off (doze_steps below zero), the Z's next step: the pictures snore_z_top and snore_z_bottom name are copied into characters $85 and $86, and z_step moves on, back to z_loop at z_end. Then doze_wait counts down, and while dozing poses remain, each run-out shows the next (monster_pose).
Low byte of the LDA operand at $9334, the upper cell's picture address, from z_frames_lo.
High byte of the upper picture's address, from z_frames_hi. The copy loop follows: eight bytes each into $5C28 and $5C30.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $933A, the lower cell's picture address.
High byte of the lower picture's address. Then the copy loop's end and the step to the next.
Copies 16 bytes, one of the monster's poses, from the address in its LDA into characters $73 and $74 ($5B98), and moves the address on 16 bytes to the next pose.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $9367, the pose's address: set by pose_reset and monster_wind, moved on 16 by monster_pose.
High byte of the pose's address. Then the store into the characters.
Points monster_pose at the first pose ($8E95).

Undoes torture_start's engine settings on the way out: the panel's and the tablet's sprites back to y $DD, $126C cleared, $24F0 set to $FF, object_collisions' slot settings back ($12DE 0, $12E6 0, $12EA 8), player_x_min $1F, player_x_limit's second byte (past 255) back to $3B, shot_y_max $BF, and the engine's solid character tests the right way round again (BCC into solid_test_bcc's five, BCS into solid_test_bcs's three).

Writes the branch opcode in A over the three branches after the engine's CMP $8B96 tests that are BCS in the engine ($2DDD, $2E47 and $AD1D in player_dead): torture_start writes BCC ($90), torture_leave BCS ($B0) back.
Writes A over the five branches after the CMP $8B96 tests that are BCC in the engine ($2CC7, $2D1D, $2D98, $2DFE and $31C1): torture_start writes BCS ($B0), torture_leave BCC ($90) back.

Puts Clyde (sprite 0) on the VIC: position, pointer and colour; unless he is riding, his two shot sprites (1 and 2) too; the ninth x bits; $D026 (the sprites' second multicolour) yellow, and all eight sprites on. raster_objects_a calls it each frame.

The green monster's round of moves, a byte each: $80-$84 start move 0-4 from the beginning of its scripts, 0-4 carry on from where the last move's scripts were left; $FF at the end moves it a pixel left (the moves add up to one pixel right) and starts the round again. Move 0 walks 16 pixels left, 1 walks 16 right, 2 stands for 8 frames, 3 stands 38 frames spitting, 4 stands 59 frames with a longer spit. Its x runs between 79 and 177.
Low bytes of the five moves' x scripts ($9495, $94A6, $94EA, $94CC, $94B7).
High bytes of the x scripts, all $94.
Low bytes of the five moves' frame scripts ($94F3 twice, $94FC, $94FE, $9507).
High bytes of the frame scripts, then from $9495 the scripts themselves.
Move 0's x script: 16 steps of $81 (a pixel left each frame), then $FF.
Move 1's x script: 16 steps of 1 (a pixel right), then $FF.
Move 4's x script: 59 frames of 0 (no movement) to the $FF at $94F2; move 3's starts inside it at $94CC (38 frames) and move 2's at $94EA (8 frames).
The frame script of moves 0 and 1, a step every sixth frame: $B3, $B5, $B7, $B9, $B7, $B5, $B3, $B1 (each with the next frame for object 1), 0 to start again.
Move 2's frame script: $B3, then 0.
Move 3's frame script: $BB, $BD, $BB, $B3, $BF, $C1, $BF, $B3, then 0; frame $C1 spits (gm_spit).
Move 4's frame script: as move 3's with $C1 held for four steps.

The green monster, each frame while Clyde is up on its ledge. Once it has been killed it finishes its move and then starts dying (gm_dying). Between moves it reads the next byte of gm_script and sets up that move's x and frame scripts (resetting their positions for $80-$84). During a move, each frame the x script's byte moves it (under $80 right by the low four bits, from $80 left), $FF ending the move; every sixth frame the frame script gives objects 0 and 1 their frames (the byte and the byte plus one), 0 starting it again.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $9570, the move's x script address, from gm_x_lo.
High byte of the x script's address, from gm_x_hi. Then the byte's meaning: $FF ends the move, under $80 adds the low four bits to the x.
Operand of the SBC at $9590: the pixels to move left, the low four bits of a byte of $80 or more.
Low byte of the LDY operand at $95B2, the move's frame script address, from gm_frames_lo.
High byte of the frame script's address. Then objects 0 and 1 take the frame and the next, or 0 starts the script again.
How far a fireball moves left at each of its steps: 3 for the first fifteen, slowing through 2 and 1 to 0; $FF at step 57 ends its flight.
How far a fireball drops at each step: 0, with ten steps of 1 among steps 13-31.
A fireball's frame at each step: blank at step 0, then $C7 and $C3-$C7 in turn, then $C8 up to $CF (without $CC), and blank again at step 56.
Set when fireball 0's flight has ended (or the flame, which uses both objects); cleared when the monster spits it.
Set when fireball 1's flight has ended, and when the flame ends.

The green monster's spit. When its frame becomes $C1 (once per showing, spit_latch), the next fireball starts: right of x $78 (120) as a fireball 5 pixels right of the monster's x and 10 lines below its top, light red; left of it as a flame instead (gm_flame). Each frame, right of x $78, each flying fireball moves by fireball_dx and fireball_dy with fireball_frames until its $FF.
Operand of the SBC at $96DC: the fireball's step left, from fireball_dx.
Operand of the ADC at $96F1: the fireball's step down, from fireball_dy. Then its frame from fireball_frames and the next step.

The spit left of x $78: objects 2 and 3 become a flame, $14 and $2C pixels left of the monster and 5 lines below its top, orange, for 28 steps (fireball_step); each frame (left of x $78) they take the next frames of Clyde's own flame (flame_frames_l1 and flame_frames_l2), and at the end both blank and both fireballs are marked done.
The three rats' starting x (low bytes), copied to rat_x by torture_start: $EE, $02 and $16 (238, and 258 and 278 with their ninth bits).
Each rat's ninth x bit in the second band's byte $C25C: $08 (object 5), $20 (object 7), $40 (object 8).
The rats' x positions (low bytes), copied into objects 5, 7 and 8 by the main loop each frame.
Rat 1's x.
Rat 2's x.
The rats' frames, copied into objects 5, 7 and 8: rat 0's.
Rat 1's frame.
Rat 2's frame.
Each rat's pseudo-random byte: times five, plus $81 (and the carry), exclusive-or $10 at each choice.
Frames until each rat chooses again: rat_decide_time each time.
How far left each rat walks on its side of x 256: $CD for rat 0, $EE for the others.
A rat's frames walking right, read from index 8 ($94, the first after a change) then 7 down to 0 over and over: $9F, $A0, $A1, $A2, $A1, $A0, $9F, $9E.
Walking left: $94, then $9A, $9B, $9C, $9D, $9C, $9B, $9A, $99.
Rats 1 and 2 gnawing the rope, facing out, mouth opening and shutting: $94, then $95, $96, $97, $98, $97, $96, $95, $94; each time round adds one to gnaw_count.
Rat 0 at the popcorn, head down: $F3, $F2, $F1 after a change, then $F2, $F3, $F4, $F3, $F2, $F1 over and over.
rat_timer's value at each choice: $25 at the start (torture_start), 1 once the popcorn has spilt (rat_target).
The rounds of gnawing for each stage of the rope: $0A (torture_start).

Rat Y, each frame. When its timer runs out it chooses: before the popcorn has spilt, at random from rat_random (under $32 sit, under $96 walk left, else walk right; the LDA #$FF for left is hidden in the BIT at $97C2); once it has spilt, rat_target walks it to its place. A change restarts its frames. Then: sitting shows $94; walking moves it a pixel every other frame between its limits (rat_left_limit, and x 315 on the right), its frame changing every fourth frame (rat_left_frames, rat_right_frames); at its place rat 0 eats (rat_eat_frames) and rats 1 and 2 gnaw (rat_gnaw_frames), and at gnaw_rounds rounds rope_stage_due is set.
Where each rat goes once the popcorn has spilt (low bytes): $FB for rat 0, $09 past 256 (265) for rat 1, $ED for rat 2: beside the popcorn (x 239), where the rope's run crosses the ledge.
The ninth x bit of each place, as rat_msb_bits would show it: only rat 1's is past 256.
The way to walk while a rat is on the other side of x 256 from its place: left for rats 0 and 2, right for rat 1.
What each rat does at its place: 2 (eat) for rat 0, 3 (gnaw) for rats 1 and 2.

rat_move's choice once the popcorn has spilt: rat_decide_time becomes 1 (the rat chooses every frame); sitting once Chaz is gone (chaz_gone); otherwise right or left towards its place, or its place's state when it is there.
The rope's three stages, counted by rope_snap: 1 frame (the weight drops a pixel), 3 frames (three pixels), then $FF (it falls).
The second and third stages' counts, 3 and $FF.

When the rats have gnawed gnaw_rounds rounds. The opcode here is SEC ($38, from torture_start) until the third stage, when it becomes CLC ($18) and the BCC after it goes to weight_fall. Otherwise: gnaw_count starts again, and the stage's count is taken down: each frame of it the weight drops a pixel and the rope runs (rope_run); at its end rope_stage moves on and rope_stage_due is cleared.

The weight falls, each frame: weight_fall_step goes down to 1 (then index 0), and the weight drops by weight_fall_dy (1 up to 8 pixels), its y also written into belt_wait so the belt stops. From the fourth frame each frame takes a cell off the rope's run and adds one to its drop (rope_lengthen), and rope_run is called the index plus one times. When the weight reaches line $B0 it lands at $B8, on the demon working the mill: weight_down, rescued, a screen shake (shake_step 7) and score value $0F (five in the hundreds digit).
Clears the next cell of the rope's run on row 8, from column 27 leftwards, and puts the drop's character $0D into the next cell of column 14, from row 13 downwards.
Low byte of the STA operand at $9958, the run's next cell: $5B (row 8, column 27, $455B) at the start, one less each call.
High byte of the run's cell, $45.
Low byte of the STA operand at $995D, the drop's next cell: $16 (row 13, column 14, $4616) at the start, $28 more each call.
High byte of the drop's cell, from $46.
The rope runs a step: character $0D's rows rotate down one (the drop), and rows 3-6 of character $08 rotate left a multicolour pixel (the run).
Clyde's collisions, each frame he is not dying: the handler is hurt_handler; the green monster (monster_test, its box 21 lines below its y), then each fireball that is not blank (fireball_tests).
Tests objects 2 and 3, the fireballs or the flame, at their positions and frames, against the box set by the caller.
Tests the green monster (object 0) with the box A picks (0 Clyde's, otherwise the shot's), at its x and its y plus $15.
The handler for Clyde touching the green monster or its fire: JMP $3CEC, player_hurt after its invulnerability test.

The tests for Clyde's shot X (0 or 2, for shot sprites 1 and 2), when it is out. While the green monster is alive: the monster (handler gm_hit), the water tank (tank_hit) and the fireballs (shot_spent at $CEC2, so a fireball stops a shot). Once it is dying: the popcorn box (box_hit) until it falls.

Puts the object under test (A = x, X = y, Y = frame) in the spare slot 15 ($C27D, $C27E, $C179), which is the only one object_collisions tests in a chamber, and sets the box: Clyde's (player_box_x, player_box_y), or shot $43's (shot_box, shot_box_y) when the operand at $9A62 is set.
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $9A61: which box, 0 for Clyde's, otherwise the shot's; written by monster_test and shot_tests.
Runs object_collisions for slot 15 with its ninth x bit ($C25E) and its tall bit ($C009) clear, the AND operands at $9A8C and $9A92 being 0.
Operand of the AND at $9A8B, 0: slot 15's ninth x bit.
Operand of the AND at $9A91, 0: slot 15's tall bit. Then object_collisions.
The handler for a shot on the water tank: the shot is spent; if the tank is upright and full, it starts to tip (tank_tipping).
The handler for a shot on the popcorn box: the shot is spent and the box moves a pixel right; at x $D0 it is off the ledge and falls (box_falling).

The handler for a shot on the green monster: the shot is spent, the monster flashes (gm_flash 9, unless already flashing) and gm_damage takes the weapon's grade plus one; at 200 it is killed (gm_killed).
gm_burst's frame index, 8 at the start, counted down.
Object 0's frames as the green monster bursts, read from the end: $B3, then $F5, $F7, $F9, $FB, $FD, $FF, and $0F (gone).
Object 1's frames as it bursts: $B4, then $F6, $F8, $FA, $FC, $FE, $FF, and $0F.

The green monster's death, every sixth frame: its two halves take the next frames of gm_burst_frames_a and b, and its normal colour becomes light red (gm_flash_colours); after the last, gm_gone is set and score value $0E is added (two in the hundreds digit).
The popcorn's pouring frames left, 6 (box_fall); at 0 the rats go to their places.

Each frame once the box has been pushed off the ledge: for 18 frames it falls and tips onto the rats' ledge (box_fall_dx, box_fall_dy, box_fall_frames); then every fourth frame the popcorn pours out (object 6, popcorn_frames) until popcorn_step reaches 0.
Returns not-equal on frames where frame_divider's $1219 and $121A are both set, every fourth frame.
The rising Z's sixteen pictures, eight bytes each, that snore_z copies into characters $85 and $86 through z_frames_lo/hi (picture 1 here, picture 16 at $9BDF).

The chamber's screen, 25 rows of 40 character codes: torture_start copies four whole pages from here into the screen at $4400, so the last 24 bytes it copies ($9FCF-$9FE6, the start of char_colours) land in the unused bytes and sprite pointers at $47E8-$47FF before the sprites are set.
The colour of each of the chamber's 256 characters: torture_start colours every cell of the screen by the character in it.
char_colours from character $31: the colours of characters $31-$FF.

The chamber's tune, started by tune_start (music_play with $A0CF), in the music driver's format: a header of two voice offsets, the three voices' streams from $A0D3, $A168 and $A2E9, and the seven sections they call, $A3E4 to $A51E.
torture_tune's first voice, to its end command at $A167; it calls sections $A44A and $A4D9.
torture_tune's second voice, to $A2E8; it calls sections $A3E4, $A4F0 and $A4FF.
torture_tune's third voice, to $A3E3; it calls sections $A3E4, $A50E and $A3F7.

torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: player_dead reads five water characters from $A300 on levels 1.1 and 1.2 only, and player_hit_object a table of harmless frames from stage 6 on, but a chamber's main loop never calls player_collisions.
torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup writes $32 here on world 2's levels; a chamber starts at its own entry ($8051) and never runs stage_main_setup.
torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: world 2's levels have a routine here, called by stage_main_setup and player_hit_world2; the chamber runs neither.
torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: player_hit_object jumps here for frame $8F from stage 6 on, but the chamber's main loop never calls player_collisions.
torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: level_player_call's operand still holds level 2.2's $A334, but torture_start sets $126C, which skips that call.
torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: level_jump_call's operand still holds level 2.2's $A36C, taken only while $122B is set, and retry_screen clears it.
The third voice from $A387: settings, a note and a call of section $A3F7, the same twelve bytes again at $A3AB, notes between; then more calls of $A3F7 and the end command at $A3E3.
torture_tune's bytes. The label is the engine's: level_anim_call's operand still holds level 2.2's $A3C6, taken only while $122B is set.
The seven sections torture_tune's voices call (music command $23), each ending in a return ($24): $A3E4, $A3F7, $A44A, $A4D9, $A4F0, $A4FF and $A50E.

torture_tune's bytes, to the end of its last section at $A51E. The label is the engine's: level_hook_call's operand still holds level 2.2's $A3FD; a chamber runs its own main loop, not the one that makes that call.
Fills both screens with character $FF, a blank, and the colour RAM with black (screen_fill), and sets 40 columns.
memory_swap 6: exchanges the text character set with the chamber's, for the Get Ready and rescue screens.
The chamber's first start, reached from the entry at $8051: weapon_setup with X = 0 and Y = 0 (weapon 0 at grade 0, the panel's icon set by loader_hand_over), then retry_screen.

The Get Ready screen before each try: clears the engine's variables $120C-$126C and sets $126D-$1272 to $FF, swaps in the text characters, draws the lives digit and GET READY, moves the panel and tablet sprites down to y $ED, points print_at's strings 5-11 at this file's texts and prints string 11, "RESCUE CHAZ AS SOON AS POSSIBLE", at $4684, starts sound effects $15 and $16, and runs the colour bars (raster_retry_bars). Fire silences it (screen_off), swaps the characters back and starts the chamber (torture_start).

The Get Ready screen's raster routine at line $69 (line $F9 the first time, where irq_install starts the chain): sixteen lines of background colour from the list for this frame (delays from colour_bar_delays); then the background and the second sprite multicolour yellow, and the lives sprite (sprite 0, block $4E, Clyde's face, light red, at x $D0, y $94), shown or hidden with frame_divider's $121B so it blinks every four frames. Next raster_retry_panel at line $C8.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $A601, the colour list's address, from retry_bars_lo.
High byte of the colour list's address, from retry_bars_hi. The code after it writes the bars, then sets up the lives sprite and counts the frame for retry_screen ($120D).
The Get Ready screen's line $F4: panel_lower and the open border. Next raster_retry_bars at line $69.
Low bytes of the seven texts at $8D3D-$8DF3 (rescue_text_1 to rescue_text_7), copied into print_at's strings 5-11.
High bytes of the seven texts, all $8D.

The rescue: plays rescue_tune and shows the dot-matrix sign spelling WELL DONE, its dots little pictures of Clyde's face. Every other frame two colour lists rotate a place: the big letters take the first list's front colour and the six story lines take successive places of the second, so the colours ripple down them. After $78 counts every other frame (about five seconds) it prints WELL DONE in big letters, the six lines of story and the potion digit 6; potion_award then counts the digit down, paying potions. Fire leaves (torture_exit).

The digit's bottom right cell takes the first list's third colour ($A821 into $DB34), then potion_award. On alternate frames the count at $A81E runs down, and when it reaches 0 print_big writes WELL DONE (string 13) at $4483, print_at the six story lines (strings 5-10) at $451F, $454B, $45BC, $45E3, $465A and $4687, and print_potion_digit the 6. Each pass ends with music_frame. The label is the engine's: object_spawn's movement script operand ($2083) still holds $A753 from the level before; nothing reads these bytes as data.
Prints big string 14, the potion digit at $ABF3, at $470B.
Silences the SID (volume 0), turns the sprites off, makes the background black and blanks the screen (screen_blank).
Leaves the rescue screen: screen_off, torture_leave; with lives left it swaps the character set back and loads the next stage (stage_next), else game_restart.

Pays the reward, once the digit has been printed (the cell at $470B is no longer $FF) and each time the flowing colours bring dark grey ($0B) to the front of story_colours (every 40 frames): the digit at $ABF3 counts down from 6 to 0; at each step potion_add adds the worth of Clyde's last potion pickup (the ADC operand at $B8B4, 1 or 5) to the kind award_kinds names and to the total. With the usual 1 that is six potions, two of each kind.
Operand of the LDY at $A807: the new digit (5 down to 0), the index into award_kinds.
For each step of potion_award (digit 0-5), the potion counter it pays into: 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3.
rescue_screen's count before the big text appears: set to $78 and counted down every other frame.

The first of twenty colours that flow along the big WELL DONE, red at the start: rescue_screen rotates the list a place every other frame, the last ($A832) moving to the front, and this front colour goes to both rows of the big letters ($D883 and $D8AB, eighteen cells each) and the digit's top left cell ($DB0B).
The list's second colour (light red at the start), the big digit's top right cell ($DB0C).
The list's third colour (yellow at the start), the digit's bottom right cell ($DB34).

The list's fourth colour on, the first of them the digit's bottom left cell ($DB33). From the start: light red, red, blue, light blue, cyan, light blue, blue, brown, orange, light red, orange, brown, dark grey, green, light green, green.
The list's last colour, dark grey at the start, which moves to the front at each rotation.
The first of twenty colours that flow down the six story lines, white at the start: it colours the first line ($D91F, 26 cells), and potion_award pays each time it is dark grey ($0B).
The second colour, the second line ($D947, 26 cells).
The third colour, the third line ($D9BC, 35 cells).
The fourth colour, the fourth line ($D9E3, 35 cells).
The fifth colour, the fifth line ($DA5A, 37 cells).
The sixth colour on, the first of them the sixth line ($DA82, 37 cells). From the start: light green, cyan, green, dark grey, black, black, brown, orange, light red, yellow, then white.
The list's last colour, white at the start, moved to the front at each rotation.

The sign's fade step, counted down from 7 to 0 every other frame by raster_rescue_top and indexing matrix_colours, matrix_mc1 and matrix_mc2: matrix_scroll sets it to 7 six frames before each letter changes, so the dots have faded to black, or nearly, when it does.
The sign's sprite colour for each fade step 0-7: light red when settled, then orange, brown, black at steps 3-5, brown and orange.
The sign's second sprite multicolour for each fade step 0-7: yellow when settled, then light red, orange, brown, black at step 4, brown, orange and light red.

The rescue screen's top raster routine (line 0, line $F9 the first time): counts the frame ($120D) and flips frame_divider's flags itself; on alternate frames it runs panel_anim from $2A19 (past its own alternate-frame test) with the face's stage $123C at $FF, and steps the fade down.

Operand of the LDA at $A880 ($121B, the third flag). Then the sign's three colours for the fade step (matrix_colours, matrix_mc1 and matrix_mc2, kept at $8952-$8954), panel_colours_slow, all eight sprites multicolour and shown, none expanded, sprite 0's ninth x bit set, the multicolours set, and the row count matrix_row ($8955) set to 5. The label is the engine's: object_spawn's colour cycle operand ($20B8) still holds $A881 from the level before.

Operand of the STA at $A8C2 (matrix_row). Then the eight sprites at y $2A (matrix_set_y) placed from matrix_xy, all showing block $4E (Clyde's face) in the sign's colour, matrix_next_y, and the top row of dots ($8D3C) switched on in $D015. Next raster_rescue_row at line $40. The label is the engine's: level_frame_call's operand still holds level 2.2's $A8C3; a chamber runs its own main loop, not the one that makes that call.

Moves the sign's sprites down $1A lines, puts them behind the characters ($D01B = $FF) and shows the next row of matrix_rows, six times, at line $40 and then the lines in matrix_lines; then raster_rescue_panel at line $E0.
The rescue screen's line $E0: panel_sprites, sprites in front again. Next raster_rescue_lower at line $F4.
The rescue screen's line $F4: panel_lower and the open border. Next raster_rescue_top at line 0.
Moves the sign's sprites' y in matrix_xy on by $20; raster_rescue_top calls it after placing the sprites, and matrix_set_y overwrites it the next frame, so it changes nothing on screen.
Sets all eight y positions in matrix_xy to A.
The sign's eight sprites, x and y: x $11C, then $FC down to $3C, 32 pixels apart, sprite 7 on the left.
The y positions in matrix_xy, set by matrix_set_y and matrix_next_y.
The raster lines of raster_rescue_row's second to sixth runs, read from the end: $5A, $74, $8E, $A8, $C2.
matrix_scroll's letter count, 9 down to 0, back to the font's start after the tenth.
Frames until the next letter: $16, so a letter every 23 frames.

Changes the sign's letter (each frame of the rescue screen): six frames before the change it starts the fade ($A847 = 7), and at the change copies the next seven-byte letter of matrix_font into matrix_rows, the letter's first byte into the top row ($8D3C), wrapping after ten.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $A9A0, the letter's address in matrix_font, moved on seven bytes a letter.
High byte of the letter's address. Then the copy into matrix_rows and the step to the next letter.
The sign's ten letters, seven rows of eight dots each, top row first: a space, W, E, L, L, a space, D, O, N, E. The same bytes as chamber 1's.

The second space's last row, then D, O, N and E. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup calls the level's code here on the first two stages (see world1_ranges); a chamber never runs stage_main_setup.

The rescue screen's tune, started by rescue_screen (music_play with $A9FF), in the music driver's format: the three voices' streams from $AA03, $AA7A and $AAE9 and three sections they call, to $ABF0. The same bytes as chamber 1's rescue tune.
Two bytes nothing reads, $14 and 0, the same as in chamber 1's file.
print_big's string 14, the potion digit ("6", $FF), counted down by potion_award.
print_big's string 13, "WELL DONE" and $FF.
The file's last byte, $BC; nothing reads it.
